Problem_Opportunity: Magnetic handshower docking is convenient but repeated docking, impact and hose loads can damage structural or wetted components.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Moen Magnetix; Delta SureDock; CT-013; ST-017; TR-050
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Separate magnetic alignment/retention from the primary structural load path and control docking impact/load transfer.
Proposed_Product_Response: Mechanically captured magnetic dock with controlled impact stop/load spreader and replaceable wear element.
User_Benefit: Easy one-handed docking with improved durability and leakage resistance.
Technology_Mechanism: Magnetic alignment + mechanical load path decoupling
Evidence_Status: EVIDENCED problem and precedent; PROPOSED architecture
Main_Uncertainty: Exact competitor failure mode and required load path remain unverified; prototype testing required.

Problem_Opportunity: Recurring mineral clogging creates repeated manual cleaning burden and spray degradation.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Rub-clean nozzles; removable spray faces; industrial fluid-driven rotating cleaning nozzles
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Use domestic shower flow to create controlled movement that mechanically disrupts deposits or promotes maintenance without external power.
Proposed_Product_Response: Compact rotating/oscillating maintenance element integrated behind or within the spray face.
User_Benefit: Potentially lower manual cleaning frequency and more stable spray performance.
Technology_Mechanism: Fluid reaction/turbine torque or hydraulic oscillation
Evidence_Source: 2026-09-20 staging; Spraying Systems TankJet D41800E; CYCO 36500
Evidence_Status: EVIDENCED industrial mechanism; UNKNOWN shower transfer
Main_Uncertainty: Domestic pressure/flow, pressure loss, scale, noise, leakage and durability.

Problem_Opportunity: Residual water on exposed spray surfaces can dry and leave mineral deposits.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Rub-clean nozzles; removable spray faces; TR-005 directional wettability/capillary surfaces
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Use engineered wettability/topography to move residual water away from the exposed face toward a controlled drain path.
Proposed_Product_Response: Patterned spray-face surface plus hidden drainage channels.
User_Benefit: Less standing water and potentially slower visible scale formation.
Evidence_Source: 2026-09-20 staging; ACS Langmuir anisotropic wetting evidence; TR-005
Main_Uncertainty: Soap, cleaners, mineral deposits, finish wear and manufacturing tolerances may degrade the effect.

Problem_Opportunity: Persistent mineral fouling may remain where passive nozzle cleaning is insufficient.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Manual descaling; rub-clean nozzles; industrial ultrasonic fouling control; TR-046
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Use localized ultrasonic excitation as an automatic anti-fouling mechanism.
Proposed_Product_Response: Compact piezoelectric element coupled to the spray module and activated intermittently.
User_Benefit: Potential reduction of deposit adhesion and maintenance frequency.
Main_Uncertainty: Energy, acoustic coupling, potable-water compatibility, noise, waterproofing, cost and actual scale effectiveness.

Problem_Opportunity: Handshower hoses can twist, protrude into the user's body path or return to an unwanted side position.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Swivel hose connectors; flexible hoses; conventional docks; GROHE Movario; TR-017
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Combine torsion decoupling with a passive hose-routing/parking geometry that biases the hose toward a controlled neutral path.
Proposed_Product_Response: Free-rotating hose interface plus compliant or guided parking channel near the wall.
User_Benefit: Less hose interference and more predictable handshower handling.
Fitting_Application: Handshower dock / wall connection / hose interface
Evidence_Status: EVIDENCED user signal and swivel precedent; PROPOSED combined architecture
Main_Uncertainty: Performance across hose stiffness, length, installation height and bathroom geometry.

Problem_Opportunity: Inlet screens/filters can accumulate debris and increase pressure loss or reduce flow.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Replaceable shower filters/screens; GEFA and Puretec automatic backflush filters
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Use pressure differential from the fixture itself to trigger a short hydraulic cleaning event without routine manual screen removal.
Proposed_Product_Response: Compact screen module with differential-pressure trigger and controlled reverse-flow discharge path.
User_Benefit: Longer stable flow and less manual screen maintenance.
Fitting_Application: Handshower inlet / showerhead filter module / serviceable screen
Evidence_Status: EVIDENCED commercial mechanism; UNKNOWN shower-scale transfer
Main_Uncertainty: Available differential pressure, backflow protection, potable-water compliance, sealing, noise and package size.

Problem_Opportunity: Water-powered fixture intelligence can power sensing/indicators but repeating the concept does not create a new user outcome.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Zurn Hydro-X; TOTO EcoPower; Hello Klean Shower Head+; TR-006
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Water-flow energy harvesting for local fixture electronics.
User_Benefit: No distinct benefit established beyond existing precedent.
Main_Uncertainty: No material new outcome or architecture identified.

Problem_Opportunity: Shower selectors/diverters can be difficult to operate with wet or soapy hands and may require excessive force.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Rotary knobs; push/pull diverters; spray-mode selectors; TR-004 bistable compliant valves
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Provide a broad low-grip input coupled to a bistable/compliant force-transmission element that snaps between defined states.
Proposed_Product_Response: Paddle/rocker or broad selector with compliant snap-through mechanism and separate low-friction valve interface.
User_Benefit: Lower hand force, easier wet-hand operation and clearer tactile confirmation.
Technology_Mechanism: Compliant bistability + force transmission / low-friction selector interface
Evidence_Source: 2026-09-22 staging; Kohler reviews; user reports; TR-004; compliant mechanism research
Evidence_Status: EVIDENCED user signal and enabling mechanism; PROPOSED combined architecture
Main_Uncertainty: Long-term hot-water/chemical/cycle durability and whether benefit exceeds a conventional large lever.

Problem_Opportunity: Selector effort can increase when water pressure acts directly on the valve element.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Industrial low-torque selector valves; pressure-balanced rotary control valves
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Use pressure-balanced or shear-seal geometry so line pressure contributes less to user actuation torque.
Proposed_Product_Response: Compact shower selector cartridge with pressure-balanced sealing surfaces and low-friction rotary interface.
User_Benefit: More predictable selector effort across domestic pressure conditions.
Evidence_Source: 2026-09-22 staging; Parker Lo-Torq; Fisher Vee-Ball; shower diverter force-reduction patent
Evidence_Status: EVIDENCED industrial mechanism; UNKNOWN shower transfer
Main_Uncertainty: Package, pressure loss, leakage after wear, potable-water materials and meaningful torque reduction at domestic pressure.

Problem_Opportunity: Residual water can remain in showerheads and discharge later, causing dripping or mineral buildup.
Existing_Solution_or_Source: Self-draining/vacuum-breaking showerhead patents; 2026-09-20 C-03 Passive Dry-Drain Spray Face
DELTA_or_Transferable_Capability: Admit air and/or open a drain path when flow stops so trapped water exits rapidly.
Proposed_Product_Response: Vacuum-break/self-drain module in the showerhead body.
User_Benefit: Reduced delayed dripping and water retention.
Technology_Mechanism: Gravity drainage + vacuum break / air admission
Evidence_Status: EVIDENCED prior art; no new architecture established
Main_Uncertainty: No materially different outcome or architecture from existing discovery/prior art.
